Manufacturer specifications for how long a particular job may take. This way the same job is charged the same in every workshop, however fast the mechanic actually was. Depending on the manufacturer, 10 or 12 AW make one hour. Formula to remember: labour charge on the invoice = number of AW × price per AW.
How often must a car go for the main inspection (HU)?
New cars for the first time after 36 months, then every 24 months. The emissions test is part of the HU.
What is a cost estimate?

An estimate of the repair costs. A non-binding estimate may only be exceeded significantly (guide value about 15 to 20 %) if the customer is informed beforehand. A binding estimate counts as a fixed price.
Explain the contractor's lien.
The workshop may keep the repaired vehicle until the invoice has been paid (§ 647 BGB).
Distinguish between registration certificate part I and part II.
Part I (formerly vehicle registration document): carry it with the vehicle. Part II (formerly vehicle title): keep it safe, important when selling, names the keeper, not necessarily the owner.
What is the CoC document?
The EU Certificate of Conformity. It confirms that the vehicle matches an approved type and is needed for first registration.
How is a workshop invoice structured?
Labour (AW × price per AW or hours × hourly rate) + parts and material − discount = net amount + 19 % VAT = invoice amount. Plus mandatory details such as date of service and tax number.
Which systems are distinguished in a vehicle?

Mechanical (e.g. cable of the parking brake), hydraulic (brakes, power steering on older vehicles), pneumatic (air brakes on trucks, air suspension), electrical and electronic (lighting, control units, ABS, ESP, electromechanical steering).
What do ABS and ESP do?
ABS stops the wheels from locking when braking, so the car can still be steered. ESP brakes individual wheels in a targeted way and so prevents skidding.
What is part of a visual inspection for road safety?
Lighting, tyres (tread legally at least 1,6 mm, damage, pressure), wipers and windows, fluid levels (brake fluid, coolant, oil), brakes, mirrors, first aid kit and warning triangle.
Why is brake fluid changed regularly?
It is hygroscopic, meaning it absorbs water. This lowers the boiling point and vapour bubbles can form, so the brakes fade. Usually changed every 2 years.
What is the CAN bus?
A data network in the vehicle through which the control units communicate. Faults are stored in the fault memory and read out with the diagnostic tester.
Distinguish between statutory warranty, a guarantee and goodwill.

Statutory warranty (liability for defects): by law, 2 years, against the seller. For used goods sold to consumers it can be shortened to 1 year if agreed expressly and separately. Guarantee: voluntary promise, usually by the manufacturer, conditions according to the guarantee certificate. Goodwill: voluntary gesture without legal entitlement, for customer loyalty.
What applies to data protection in customer service?

Use customer data only for the agreed purpose (e.g. order, invoice). Advertising by e-mail, phone or text message generally requires consent (exception: existing customers under § 7 (3) UWG). The customer can object to any advertising. Store data securely, do not pass it to unauthorised persons, delete it after the retention periods (GDPR).
How are end-of-life vehicles disposed of?
Only via an approved dismantling company or collection point. The keeper receives a certificate of destruction, which is needed for deregistration. Manufacturers must take back their vehicles.
What applies to used batteries and used oil?

Starter batteries: take-back obligation, 7,50 € deposit if no old battery is returned. Used oil: whoever sells engine oil must offer a collection point for the same amount of used oil. Store separately and leak-proof.
How does a dealership measure service quality?
Customer satisfaction surveys (e.g. a call after the workshop visit), complaint management, keeping to deadlines and cost ranges, repeat repairs, manufacturer standards.
What is an ABC analysis in the parts store?

Classifying items by their share of consumption value: A items = few items with a high value share (plan precisely, keep stock tight), C items = many items with a low value share (simplified planning), B items in between.
Which stocktaking methods are there?

Year-end stocktaking (physical count on the balance sheet date), shifted-date inventory (up to 3 months before or 2 months after the date, value rolled forward or back), perpetual inventory (continuous stock records, each item counted once a year), sample-based inventory (statistical methods).
Explain what average stock, average storage period and storage interest rate tell you.

Average stock shows the capital tied up in the warehouse. Using the 12 month-end stocks it is more precise than using only opening and closing stock. The storage period says how many days goods stay in stock on average. The storage interest rate shows how much interest the tied-up capital costs during this time: the shorter the storage period, the lower it is. Formula to remember: average stock = (opening stock + 12 month-end stocks) ÷ 13, simplified (opening + closing) ÷ 2; storage period = 360 ÷ turnover rate; storage interest rate = annual interest rate × storage period ÷ 360.
What does „delivered“ (Frei Haus) mean compared with „ex works“ (Ab Werk)?

Delivered (Frei Haus): the seller bears the transport costs up to the buyer. Between merchants, without a special agreement, the risk passes on handover to the carrier. Ex works (Ab Werk): from the seller's warehouse, the buyer bears costs and risk.
Which defect rights does the buyer have, and in what order?
First subsequent performance (repair or replacement). Only if this fails or is refused do withdrawal, price reduction and damages come into play.
Name methods of handling objections.

Yes-but method (agree, then counter-argument), boomerang method (objection becomes a buying argument), counter-question method (ask for the reason), pre-emption method (raise the expected objection yourself), reference method (satisfied customers as proof). Never dismiss objections.
What HU interval applies to taxis and other vehicles used for commercial passenger transport?
Every year, i.e. 12 months.
Which items does the EU tyre label show?

Fuel efficiency (rolling resistance), wet grip and external rolling noise (decibels and class A to C). Since 2021, where applicable, also symbols for snow and ice grip and a QR code for the EU product database.
How do you mention the price skilfully?

State the price only once the benefit is clear. Sandwich method: embed the price between two benefit arguments. Break the price into small units (e.g. per month or per 1,000 km). State the price confidently and without apologising.
What is the legal minimum tread depth for passenger cars?
1.6 mm, measured in the main groove.
What does the Blue Angel label mean?
An environmental label for products with a lower environmental impact, for paper for example made from waste paper.
How are room and heating costs allocated to departments?

Room and heating costs depend on how much floor area a department uses. So they are allocated by square metres: the more area, the more costs. Electricity is allocated more precisely by meter readings if there are separate meters. Formula to remember: total costs / total area × area of the department.
Distinguish between gross margin and mark-up.

Both describe the same amount between landed cost and selling price, but with a different base. The mark-up refers to the landed cost (purchasing view: how much do I add?). The margin refers to the selling price (sales view: how much of the price do I keep?). That is why the mark-up is always higher than the margin: a 25 % mark-up equals a 20 % margin. Formula to remember: mark-up = margin × 100 / (100 − margin); margin = mark-up × 100 / (100 + mark-up).
Explain which type of calculation applies at which step in backward calculation.

Customer discount and cash discount: deduct as a percentage of the price (× 0.9 etc.). Profit and overheads: work back by dividing by (1 + rate). Delivery costs: subtract. Supplier cash discount and discount: divide by (1 − rate).
Describe the structure of the cost-plus calculation for a workshop job.

Productive wages (hours × wage rate) + workshop overhead mark-up (rate from the cost allocation sheet, based on productive wages) = total cost + profit mark-up = net price for the labour. Parts are usually charged separately at their selling price.
Distinguish between pre-calculation and post-calculation and state their purpose.

Pre-calculation: before the job, using planned values (standard costs), to set the quoted price or cost estimate. Post-calculation: after the job, using actual values (actual costs), to identify variances and the actual result.
Explain mixed (compensatory) pricing.

Some products are sold at a low margin because of competition (e.g. new cars, special offers). Others with a higher margin (e.g. accessories, parts, service) make up for it. What matters is that the overall range covers all costs and makes a profit.
Describe what applies to declining-balance depreciation for acquisitions from July 2025.

For movable fixed assets acquired from July 2025 to December 2027: a fixed percentage of the remaining book value, at most three times the straight-line rate and no more than 30%. Pro rata by month in the first year. Switching to straight-line is allowed; switching back is not.
Explain the collective item (pool depreciation).

An optional alternative to the low-value asset rule: fixed assets from €250.01 to €1,000 net are grouped into one pool per year and depreciated at 20% a year over 5 years, even if an asset leaves earlier. The choice applies uniformly to all assets of this size in the financial year.
Describe how the sale of a fixed asset at a gain or loss is recorded.

The net selling price is compared with the remaining book value. If it is higher, there is a gain on disposal; if lower, a loss. The remaining book value is derecognised, and VAT is charged on the selling price.
Distinguish between accounting and imputed depreciation.

Accounting: based on acquisition cost, under commercial and tax law, over the standard useful life from the depreciation table; recorded in the P&L. Imputed: based on replacement value, over the actual useful life, continuing after the book value reaches zero; used in cost accounting and pricing.
Explain workshop utilisation, efficiency and productivity.

The three ratios show where time is lost in the workshop. Utilisation shows how much of the attendance time was spent on customer jobs (the rest is idle time, tidying up, training). Efficiency shows how fast the work was done: more sold than clocked hours means faster than the standard time. Productivity combines both: how much of the paid attendance could be sold? Formula to remember: utilisation = clocked / attendance hours; efficiency = sold / clocked hours; productivity = sold / attendance hours = utilisation × efficiency; each × 100.
Describe how to determine the hourly labour rate from workshop costs.

The rate must cover all workshop costs, spread over the hours that can really be sold to customers. So you divide all workshop costs (productive and unproductive wages, overheads, allocations from the cost allocation sheet) by the saleable hours and add the profit mark-up. Formula to remember: saleable hours = attendance hours × utilisation × efficiency.
Describe the steps of workshop job control.

Appointment and capacity planning, vehicle check-in with the customer, signed repair order (with cost estimate if needed), job allocation to mechanics, execution with time recording, customer approval for extra work, quality check, invoice, vehicle handover with explanation, follow-up.
Name the conditions under which a dealership may deduct input VAT.

The supply was received for the business, there is a proper invoice showing VAT separately, and the supply has been made. No deduction where the purchase is used for VAT-exempt sales (e.g. insurance brokerage) or where no VAT is shown, e.g. when buying a used car from a private seller.
Name the mandatory details of an invoice.

Name and address of supplier and recipient, tax number or VAT ID, issue date, sequential invoice number, quantity and type of supply, date of supply, net amount by tax rate, tax rate and tax amount (or a note on the exemption). Small invoices up to €250 gross need fewer details.
Describe what applies to e-invoicing between businesses (B2B).

Since 2025 all businesses must be able to receive e-invoices. Businesses with prior-year turnover above €800,000 must issue them from 2027, all businesses from 2028. An e-invoice is a structured format (e.g. XRechnung, ZUGFeRD); a plain PDF does not count. Small invoices up to €250 are exempt.
Explain when the new and used car sales conditions (NWVB/GWVB) apply to a purchase contract.

They are standard terms and conditions (a non-binding recommendation by the trade associations). They apply only if properly incorporated: express reference when the contract is concluded, a reasonable opportunity to read them and the customer's consent (§ 305(2) BGB). Individual agreements take precedence (§ 305b BGB).
Describe how a used car purchase contract is concluded under the GWVB.

The buyer's order is the offer; the buyer is bound by it for at most 10 days (commercial vehicles 2 weeks). The contract is formed when the seller confirms acceptance in text form within this period or delivers the vehicle.
Describe the buyer's rights if delivery of the new car is delayed.

With a non-binding date, the buyer can demand delivery no earlier than six weeks after it has passed, which puts the seller in default (with a binding date, immediately). The buyer can then set a reasonable additional period and withdraw from the contract once it has expired without result (§ 323 BGB); if the seller is at fault, damages can also be claimed.
Describe what applies if the buyer does not take delivery of the ordered vehicle.

The buyer must take delivery within the agreed period after receiving the notice of readiness. If not, the seller can withdraw after an unsuccessful deadline and claim damages. The sales conditions provide a lump-sum percentage of the purchase price for this; the buyer may prove that the loss was lower (§ 309 No. 5 BGB).
Assess whether the buyer may transfer rights under the new car purchase contract to a third party.
Under the NWVB only with the seller's prior consent. This allows the dealer to prevent ordered vehicles from being passed on to resellers, for example.
Explain when there is a material defect under § 434 BGB.

When, at the passing of risk, the item does not meet the subjective requirements (agreed quality, use assumed under the contract), the objective requirements (suitability for ordinary use, customary quality) or the assembly requirements. With consumers, a negative deviation is valid only if they were specifically informed and it was agreed expressly and separately (§ 476(1) BGB).
Distinguish between a complaint and an exchange.

Complaint: the goods are defective and the customer has statutory warranty rights (subsequent performance first). Exchange: the goods are free of defects, there is no legal right; an exchange is a goodwill gesture. Exception: 14-day right of withdrawal for distance and off-premises contracts.
When is a customer in default of payment and what follows?

Default after a reminder, without a reminder if a calendar date was fixed, at the latest 30 days after due date and receipt of the invoice (consumers only if the invoice says so). Consequences: default interest (consumers 5, businesses 9 percentage points above the base rate), compensation for damage caused by the delay, and a flat €40 fee towards businesses.
Name special warranty rules for consumer sales.

Limitation period generally 2 years from handover. For used goods (e.g. used cars) it can be shortened to 1 year, but only by an express, separate agreement. Reversed burden of proof: if a defect appears within one year, it is presumed to have existed at handover.
How does the workshop handle waste correctly?

Order of priority: avoid, reuse, recycle, otherwise recover, dispose. Collect waste separately (used oil, oil filters, brake fluid, coolant, batteries, oily rags) and do not mix it. Hand over hazardous waste only to licensed disposal companies with documentation; the business remains responsible as the waste producer.
What applies to refrigerant from the air-conditioning system?

Refrigerant must not be released into the environment. Extraction, recycling and refilling only with a suitable A/C service unit and only by staff with a certificate of competence. Old refrigerant is collected and disposed of properly.
Explain what church tax in the payslip is calculated on.
On the wage tax, not on the gross salary. In Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg it is 8 %, in the other states 9 % of the wage tax.
Assess whether a tax allowance also reduces social security contributions.

No. The allowance only reduces taxable pay and therefore the tax. Social security is calculated on the gross salary subject to social security, i.e. salary plus, for example, the employer contribution to capital-forming benefits.
Explain who pays the childless surcharge for long-term care insurance.
The employee alone. Childless employees aged 23 and over pay 0,6 % more, so their share rises from 1,8 % to 2,4 %. The employer share stays at 1,8 %.
Describe how to get from gross salary to net pay.

First work out the gross subject to social security. From it you deduct the taxes (wage tax, solidarity surcharge, church tax), which depend on taxable pay, and the employee shares of health, care, pension and unemployment insurance, which are calculated on the SV gross. Scheme to remember: SV gross − taxes − social security = net pay.
Assess a liquidity level 2 of 60 % at a dealership.

Without sales, the dealership can only pay 60 % of its short-term debts from cash and receivables; the 100 % rule of thumb is not reached. At a dealership this is not immediately dangerous, because vehicles can quickly be turned into cash as long as days in stock are short. Measures: reduce days in stock, collect receivables faster, refinance short-term loans.
Name measures a dealership can take to raise its equity ratio.

Do not distribute profits but retain them in the business. Partner contributions or new partners. Reduce debt, e.g. through smaller vehicle stocks and shorter days in stock. Sell assets that are not needed and repay debts.
Explain how to assess a ratio in the exam.

First state the value, then compare it with a benchmark: previous year (time comparison), other dealerships or the industry (company and industry comparison) or a rule of thumb. Then describe the consequence for the dealership and suggest a suitable measure.
Return on equity rises while return on sales falls. Explain how this fits together.

Return on sales relates profit to revenue, return on equity relates it to equity. If revenue rises sharply and profit only a little, return on sales falls. If at the same time equity has fallen, for example through withdrawals, or profit has risen slightly, return on equity still rises.
Name advantages and disadvantages of a lot of debt for a dealership.

Advantages: larger vehicle stocks and investments possible, positive leverage as long as return on total capital is above the interest rate, interest reduces taxable profit. Disadvantages: interest and repayment burden, dependence on banks and the manufacturer's bank, risk if interest rises or sales fall, poorer creditworthiness.
Distinguish between the target and the actual workshop index.

The target index is planned: target labour revenue (cost plus profit and risk, both calculated on cost) divided by productive wages. The actual index is what was really achieved: actual labour revenue divided by productive wages. If the actual index is below the target index, the workshop earned less than planned, for example through discounts, unbilled working time or hourly rates that are too low. It then does not fully cover its costs and the planned profit.
Explain how overheads are distributed to the cost centres in the BAB.

Costs that can be assigned directly are distributed per receipts, e.g. salaries per payroll or depreciation per asset register. The remaining costs are split with an allocation key that reflects causation as well as possible, e.g. rent by floor area or energy by share of consumption. Then the totals are formed, the service cost centre administration is allocated to the main cost centres (e.g. in the ratio of sales revenue), and the overhead rate is calculated for each main cost centre: overheads ÷ allocation base × 100.

An invalid clause makes the whole contract void
AGB save negotiation effort
Merchants must always accept others' AGB

Withdrawal
Price reduction
Supplementary performance
Damages instead of performance

allowed with the customer's consent
not allowed
only allowed for goods under 500 €

With transfer of ownership by way of security …

a receivable is assigned

per head
4 % on the contribution, rest per head
according to shares held
in a reasonable ratio

take out a loan
hire employees
sell a business property
purchase goods
Selling or encumbering land only with special authority.
An employee with general „Handlungsvollmacht“ may, without special authority, …
take out a loan
conduct a lawsuit
issue invoices
sign with ppa.

1 January to 31 March
1 March to 31 May
1 October to 30 November

Previous years' consumption, adjusted for current developments
The highest monthly consumption of last summer
The minimum order quantity of the cheapest supplier
The storage space that happens to be free right now
Demand planning is based on past figures and takes the season, vehicle base and trends into account.
Which term belongs to the EU tyre label?
Lifetime in kilometres
Wet grip
Price
Year of manufacture
The label shows fuel efficiency, wet grip and rolling noise.
What does ESP do?
It only prevents wheel lock under braking
It stabilises the vehicle when skidding through targeted braking
It controls steering
It switches the lights on
ESP intervenes when the vehicle is about to leave its course.
A supplier sells the same part it delivers to the vehicle manufacturer in its own packaging without the manufacturer's logo. What are such parts called?
Identical (OE supplier) parts
Replica (imitation) parts
Used parts
Remanufactured exchange parts
Identical parts come from the original equipment supplier and match the original part; replica parts are made by other manufacturers.
Which rule applies to the probationary period in a vocational training relationship?
at least 1 month, at most 6 months
at least 3 months, at most 6 months
at least 1 month, at most 4 months
freely agreed, at most 12 months
Section 20 BBiG: The probationary period lasts at least one month and at most four months.
A trainee wants to terminate her training contract during the probationary period. What applies?
with four weeks' notice and written reasons
at any time without notice or reasons, but in writing
only with the prior consent of the IHK
verbally with two weeks' notice
Section 22 (1) and (3) BBiG: During probation either party may terminate at any time without notice; the termination must be in writing.
Which agreement in a vocational training contract is void?
a probationary period of three months
the duty to keep a training record
a contractual penalty if the training is ended early
the scheduling of daily training hours
Section 12 (2) BBiG: Contractual penalties and payments for the training itself may not be agreed; such clauses are void.
A trainee passes the final exam in June; his contract runs until 31 July. When does the training relationship end?
on 31 July, as agreed in the contract
when the examination board announces the result
when the vocational school certificate is handed over
at the end of the month after the exam
Section 21 (2) BBiG: If the trainee passes before the end of the training period, the relationship ends when the examination board announces the result.
A trainee fails the final exam. What applies?
The training is automatically extended by exactly six months
At her request, the training is extended until the next resit, by one year at most
The company alone decides whether the training is extended
The training ends; a resit is only possible as an external candidate
Section 21 (3) BBiG: At the trainee's request, the training relationship is extended until the next resit, but by no more than one year.
An employment contract provides for a six-month probationary period. What notice period applies during this time if no collective agreement applies?
four weeks to the 15th or end of month
two weeks
one month to the end of the month
no notice period at all
Section 622 (3) BGB: During an agreed probationary period of up to six months, the notice period is two weeks.
An employee has worked for the company for one year and wants to resign effective 31 May. By when must the employer receive the notice at the latest (no special rules)?
on 30 April
on 3 May
on 17 May
on 31 March
Section 622 (1) BGB: The basic notice period is four weeks (28 days) to the 15th or the end of a month; 28 days before 31 May is 3 May.
When does general protection against dismissal under the Protection Against Dismissal Act (KSchG) apply?
from the first working day, regardless of company size
only after two years in businesses with more than 20 employees
only in businesses with a works council, regardless of duration
after more than six months in a business with more than ten employees
Sections 1 and 23 KSchG: The employment must have lasted more than six months and the business must normally have more than ten employees.
Within what period must an employee file an unfair dismissal claim with the labour court?
two weeks after the last working day
one month after receiving the notice
three weeks after receiving the written notice
six months after the end of employment
Section 4 KSchG: The claim must be filed within three weeks of receipt; otherwise the dismissal is deemed effective (Section 7 KSchG).
An employer dismisses an employee by e-mail with a scanned signature. The dismissal is …
invalid because the written form is missing
valid as soon as the e-mail has been read
valid if the works council agrees
only contestable within three weeks
Section 623 BGB: Terminating an employment relationship requires written form with a handwritten signature; electronic form is excluded.
A trainee is 16 years old at the start of the calendar year. What is his minimum holiday entitlement under the Youth Employment Protection Act (JArbSchG)?
30 working days
25 working days
27 working days
24 working days
Section 19 JArbSchG: Anyone who is not yet 17 at the start of the calendar year is entitled to at least 27 working days (Werktage) of leave.
What is the minimum uninterrupted rest period an adult employee must generally have after the end of the daily working time?
8 hours
11 hours
10 hours
12 hours
Section 5 (1) ArbZG: at least eleven hours of uninterrupted rest; for young people Section 13 JArbSchG even requires twelve hours.
Which statement about the protection periods under the Maternity Protection Act (MuSchG) is correct?
After childbirth there is generally an eight-week ban on employment
Before childbirth the woman may not work even at her own request
The woman can shorten the protection period after childbirth herself
The protection periods only apply to women in full-time employment
Section 3 MuSchG: Six weeks before childbirth (work possible at her express request) and generally eight weeks after it (ban on employment).
What is the maximum parental leave (Elternzeit) each parent can take for one child?
up to 14 months
up to two years
up to twelve months
up to three years
Section 15 (2) BEEG: up to three years per parent; up to 24 months of this can be taken between the child's 3rd and 8th birthday.
From what point can a works council be elected in a business?
at least ten employees, all of whom are of age
at least five permanent employees entitled to vote, three of them eligible for election
20 employees and only with the employer's consent
at least three employees if a collective agreement applies
Section 1 (1) BetrVG: in businesses with normally at least five permanent employees entitled to vote, three of whom are eligible for election.
An employer dismisses an employee without first consulting the existing works council. The dismissal is …
invalid because the consultation is missing
valid, but the works council can contest it
valid if there is a reason for dismissal
invalid only during the probationary period
Section 102 (1) BetrVG: The works council must be consulted before every dismissal; a dismissal without consultation is invalid.
In which matter does the works council have a genuine right of co-determination?
purchase of a new workshop building
setting the selling prices for new cars
choice of the car brands the dealer represents
start and end of daily working hours
Section 87 (1) No. 2 BetrVG: Social matters such as the scheduling of working hours require co-determination; business decisions are made by the employer alone.
A trainee is a member of the youth and trainee representation (JAV). How can he secure being kept on after his training?
As a JAV member he is automatically kept on for a fixed two years
He requests continued employment in writing within the last three months of training
He must first apply to the labour court for continued employment
As a JAV member he has no special protection regarding being kept on
Section 78a BetrVG: If he requests continued employment in writing within the last three months, a permanent employment relationship is deemed to exist.
Who concludes a company-level collective agreement (Firmentarifvertrag)?
a trade union and an individual employer
the works council and the employer
an employers' association and the IHK
the federal government and a trade union
Section 2 (1) TVG: Parties to collective agreements are trade unions, individual employers and employers' associations; works council and employer conclude works agreements.
A collective agreement provides for 30 days of leave. The employment contract of an employee covered by it states 32 days. What applies?
32 days, because deviations in the employee's favour are allowed
30 days, because the collective agreement always takes precedence
24 working days under the Federal Leave Act
31 days as the average of both rules
Section 4 (3) TVG (favourability principle): Deviations from the collective agreement are allowed if they are more favourable to the employee.
What characterises a warning strike (Warnstreik)?
a short work stoppage during negotiations after the peace obligation has ended
an indefinite strike after a successful strike ballot
a lockout of the workforce by the employers
a strike while the valid collective agreement is still running
Warning strikes are short, time-limited work stoppages that put pressure on ongoing collective bargaining; they are only permitted once the peace obligation has ended.
Which contribution does an employee usually pay alone?
the contribution to statutory accident insurance
the additional contribution to health insurance
the contribution to unemployment insurance
the surcharge for childless persons in long-term care insurance

Section 58 (1) SGB XI: The surcharge for childless members is paid by the employee alone; the health insurance additional contribution is shared equally, accident insurance is paid by the employer only.
Which requirement is part of the entitlement to unemployment benefit (ALG I)?
at least twelve months of compulsory insurance within the last 30 months
at least five years of pension insurance contributions
proven need after a check of one's own assets
a dismissal initiated exclusively by the employer
Sections 137, 142, 143 SGB III: unemployment, registering as unemployed and a qualifying period of twelve months within a 30-month reference period.
To whom does the employer transfer the total social security contribution of an employee subject to compulsory insurance?
to the tax office together with the wage tax
to the employee's health insurance fund as collecting agency
separately to each branch of insurance
to the Federal Employment Agency

Section 28h SGB IV: The health insurance fund collects the contributions for health, long-term care, pension and unemployment insurance and passes them on; accident insurance is paid by the employer to the Berufsgenossenschaft.
Which statement about a limited partner (Kommanditist) in a KG is correct?
He manages the business and is liable without limit with his private assets
He represents the KG alone and is liable only with his contribution
He is excluded from management and is liable only up to his contribution
He is liable without limit but is excluded from management
Sections 164, 170, 171 HGB: The limited partner is excluded from management and representation; he is liable only up to the amount of his contribution.
Who appoints the management board (Vorstand) of a stock corporation (AG)?
the general meeting of shareholders
the supervisory board
the works council
the registry court
Section 84 AktG: The supervisory board appoints the management board (for up to five years); the general meeting elects the shareholder representatives on the supervisory board.
What is specifically required of an entrepreneurial company (UG haftungsbeschränkt)?
The shareholders are also liable with their private assets
The share capital must be at least €25,000
A quarter of the annual net profit must be transferred to a reserve
It may employ no more than ten staff
Section 5a (3) GmbHG: A UG can be founded with very little share capital but must put 25% of its annual net profit (less any loss carried forward) into a statutory reserve each year.

An owner internally forbids his authorised signatory (Prokurist) to buy vehicles costing more than €50,000. The Prokurist nevertheless buys a vehicle for €60,000; the seller knows nothing of the ban. The purchase contract is …
void, because the Prokurist exceeded his authority
provisionally invalid until the owner approves it
voidable by the owner on grounds of mistake
valid, because the restriction has no effect on third parties
Section 50 (1) HGB: A restriction of the Prokura has no effect on third parties; internally, however, the Prokurist may be liable for damages.
A six-year-old buys a comic with his own pocket money. The purchase contract is …
void, because he lacks legal capacity
valid under the pocket-money rule (Section 110 BGB)
provisionally invalid until approved
valid because it is an everyday transaction
Sections 104, 105 BGB: Children under seven lack legal capacity and their declarations are void; Section 110 BGB applies only to persons with limited capacity.
In a written offer a salesperson mistakenly writes €18,900 instead of €19,800. The customer accepts immediately. What can the salesperson do?
avoid the contract for fraudulent deception within one year
nothing, because a typing error is never grounds for avoidance
withdraw from the contract without reason within 14 days
avoid the contract without delay due to an error in declaration
Sections 119 (1), 121 BGB: A slip of the pen is an error in declaration; avoidance must be declared without undue delay, and reliance damages may have to be paid (Section 122 BGB).
A workshop invoice becomes due on 15 March 2026; the creditor knows all relevant facts. When does the claim become time-barred (standard limitation period)?
at the end of 31 December 2029
on 15 March 2029
at the end of 31 December 2028
on 15 March 2028
Sections 195, 199 BGB: The standard limitation period is three years and starts at the end of the year in which the claim arose (here 31 Dec 2026).
A debtor makes a part payment on an outstanding claim. What effect does this have on the limitation period?
The limitation period is only suspended
The limitation period is halved
The limitation period is unaffected
The limitation period starts again
Section 212 (1) No. 1 BGB: An acknowledgement, e.g. by part payment, restarts the limitation period; negotiations or a lawsuit only suspend it.
In which case does a consumer have a statutory right of withdrawal?
She orders winter tyres from an online shop
She buys a used car on site at a car dealership
She buys a bicycle from a private individual
She buys a TV in an electronics store
Sections 312c, 312g, 355 BGB: Distance contracts between a business and a consumer carry a 14-day right of withdrawal; purchases in a shop or between private persons do not.
When does the 14-day withdrawal period start for goods bought online (assuming proper information on the right of withdrawal)?
when the consumer has received the goods
when the order is sent
when the purchase price is paid
when the retailer dispatches the goods
Section 356 (2) and (3) BGB: For a consumer sale the period starts once the consumer has received the goods, and not before proper information on withdrawal has been given.
For which goods ordered online is there no statutory right of withdrawal?
floor mats from the retailer's standard range
custom-made seat covers with an embroidered name
a roof rack in its original packaging
a child seat that was unpacked for inspection
Section 312g (2) No. 1 BGB: There is no right of withdrawal for goods made to the customer's specifications or clearly tailored to personal needs.
Household incomes rise significantly. What is the effect on the market for new cars, all other things being equal?
The supply curve shifts right; the price falls
The demand curve shifts left; the price falls
The demand curve shifts right; price and quantity rise
The supply curve shifts left; the quantity rises
For normal goods, demand rises with income; the demand curve shifts to the right and the equilibrium price and quantity rise.
The price of fuel rises by 10% and the quantity demanded falls by only 2%. Demand is …
elastic
perfectly elastic
inelastic
perfectly inelastic

The percentage change in quantity (2%) is smaller than the change in price (10%), so the price elasticity is below 1 in absolute terms. It would be perfectly inelastic only if quantity did not react at all.
How does a monopoly supplier differ from a supplier in a polypoly?
He must accept the market price as given
He can set price and quantity sold at the same time
He is not subject to supervision by the cartel office
He can set the price; demand then determines the quantity sold
The monopolist is a price setter: he sets the price (or the quantity) and buyers react. A supplier in a perfect polypoly is a quantity adjuster (price taker).
What is meant by stagflation?
strong growth combined with falling prices
falling prices combined with rising unemployment
weak or no growth combined with rising prices
stable prices combined with full employment
Stagflation = stagnation + inflation: the economy hardly grows but prices still rise, e.g. after sharp energy price increases.
The consumer price index rises from 120.0 to 123.6 points within one year. What is the inflation rate?
(123.6 − 120.0) ÷ 120.0 × 100 = 3.0%. The difference in index points is not the inflation rate.
Due to the switch to electric cars, jobs at suppliers of combustion engines are permanently lost. What type of unemployment is this?
seasonal unemployment
frictional unemployment
structural unemployment
cyclical unemployment
Structural unemployment results from lasting change in industries, technology or demand; it does not disappear with the next upswing.
Which tax is an indirect tax?
wage tax
income tax
corporation tax
VAT (Umsatzsteuer)
With indirect taxes, the taxpayer (the business) and the person who bears the tax (the end consumer) differ; VAT is passed on to the customer through the price.
Who makes up the ECB Governing Council, which decides on key interest rates?
the finance ministers of all EU member states
the heads of government of the euro countries together with the EU Commission
the boards of the major commercial banks of the euro area
the ECB Executive Board and the governors of the euro area national central banks
The Governing Council consists of the six members of the Executive Board and the governors of the national central banks of the euro countries; it is independent of governments.
Which three dimensions make up the concept of sustainable development?
regional, national, international
ecological, economic, social
short-term, medium-term, long-term
procurement, production, sales
According to the three-pillar model, environment, economy and society must be considered together so that future generations can also meet their needs.
A customer wants to have his old car scrapped. What does the End-of-Life Vehicles Ordinance (AltfahrzeugV) require?
Handing it to an authorised collection point or dismantler in return for a certificate of destruction
Handing it to any scrap dealer; no certificate is needed
Returning the vehicle to the manufacturer at the owner's own expense
Dismantling it yourself and disposing of the remains with household waste
End-of-life vehicles may only be handed over to recognised collection or take-back points or dismantling facilities; the certificate of destruction is presented when deregistering the vehicle.
To sign up for its newsletter, a car dealership asks for name, e-mail, date of birth, income and religion. Which GDPR principle is being violated?
storage limitation
accuracy of data
data portability
data minimisation
Art. 5 (1) (c) GDPR: Only data necessary for the purpose may be collected; an e-mail address is sufficient for a newsletter.
A customer asks the dealership which data it stores about him. Within what period must the dealership generally respond?
within 72 hours
within six weeks
within one year
within one month
Art. 15 and Art. 12 (3) GDPR: Information must be provided without undue delay and within one month at the latest; an extension is only possible in justified exceptional cases.
A laptop with unencrypted customer data is stolen. By when must the company normally report this to the data protection supervisory authority?
within 14 days of the theft
within one month of becoming aware
if possible within 72 hours of becoming aware
only if customers complain
Art. 33 GDPR: Notification without undue delay and where feasible within 72 hours, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the persons concerned.
Who must carry out the risk assessment of workplaces under the Occupational Safety and Health Act (ArbSchG)?
the works council
the employer
the Berufsgenossenschaft (accident insurer)
each employee individually
Sections 3, 5 ArbSchG: The employer must identify hazards and set protective measures; he may obtain advice but remains responsible.
In the workshop there is a round blue sign with a white ear-protection symbol. This is a …
mandatory sign
prohibition sign
warning sign
emergency/escape sign
ASR A1.3: blue = mandatory action, red = prohibition or fire protection, yellow = warning, green = rescue and first aid.
A sole trader's equity is €380,000 at the start of the year and €420,000 at the end. During the year he withdrew €30,000 and contributed €10,000. What is the profit?
Profit = closing equity − opening equity + withdrawals − contributions = 420,000 − 380,000 + 30,000 − 10,000 = €60,000.

Account 1400 Receivables shows: opening balance €48,000, increases €210,000, decreases €195,000. What is the closing balance and on which side of account 1400 is it entered when the account is closed?
€63,000 on the credit side
€63,000 on the debit side
€33,000 on the credit side
€453,000 on the debit side

Asset account: opening balance + increases − decreases = €63,000. The account has a debit balance. The closing balance is entered on the smaller side to balance it, i.e. the credit side of account 1400 (contra entry on the debit side of the closing balance account).
At year end, total income is €1,910,000 and total expenses are €1,840,000. Which closing entry is correct?
Equity to Profit and loss account €70,000
Profit and loss account to Closing balance account €70,000
Profit and loss account to Equity €3,750,000
Profit and loss account to Equity €70,000
Income exceeds expenses, so the profit is €70,000. The balance is on the debit side of the P&L account and increases equity on the credit side.
In the advance return period, output VAT is €4,200 and input VAT is €5,100. What is the result?
A VAT payable of €900
An input VAT surplus of €900, i.e. a claim against the tax office
A VAT payable of €9,300
No effect, because the amounts cancel out
If input VAT exceeds output VAT, the company is entitled to a refund: 5,100 − 4,200 = €900.
A customer receives an invoice on credit for €30,000 net plus 19% VAT. What is the journal entry (1400 receivables, 8000 revenue, 1770 output VAT, 1570 input VAT)?
8000 Revenue new cars €30,000 and 1770 Output VAT €5,700 to 1400 Trade receivables €35,700
1400 Trade receivables €35,700 to 8000 Revenue new cars €35,700
1400 Trade receivables €30,000 and 1570 Deductible input VAT €5,700 to 8000 Revenue new cars €35,700
1400 Trade receivables €35,700 to 8000 Revenue new cars €30,000 and 1770 Output VAT €5,700
Receivables increase on the debit side by the gross amount; revenue (net) and output VAT (30,000 × 19% = €5,700) are credited.

A vehicle lift has a list price of €25,000 net. The supplier grants a 4% discount, and 2% cash discount is deducted on payment. Freight and installation cost €1,200 net. Useful life 8 years, acquired in April. What is the straight-line depreciation in the first year?

A tow truck (acquisition cost €50,000, useful life 10 years) is acquired in January 2026 and depreciated on a declining-balance basis at the highest permitted rate. What is the depreciation in year 2?

For acquisitions from July 2025 to December 2027, the rate is at most three times the straight-line rate and no more than 30%. Year 1: €15,000; year 2: 30% of the remaining book value of €35,000 = €10,500.
A dealership's operationally necessary capital is €800,000 and the imputed interest rate is 6%. How much is the imputed interest per year?
Imputed interest = operationally necessary capital × interest rate = 800,000 × 6% = €48,000. It also covers interest on equity.

In the cost allocation sheet, €60,000 of costs from the service cost centre Administration are allocated by headcount: new cars 4, used cars 2, parts and accessories 3, workshop 11. How much does the workshop receive?
€60,000 / 20 employees = €3,000 per employee, × 11 = €33,000.

According to the cost allocation sheet, the workshop has €540,000 of overheads and €300,000 of productive wages. A job takes 4 hours at €30 productive wage per hour, and the profit mark-up is 10%. What is the net price for the labour?
Overhead rate = 540,000 / 300,000 = 180%. Wages €120 + €216 overheads = €336 total cost + 10% profit = €369.60.

Forward calculation for a roof box: list purchase price €400, supplier discount 20%, supplier cash discount 2%, delivery costs €12, overhead mark-up 30%, profit 10%, customer cash discount 2%, no customer discount. What is the net selling price on credit terms?

Net purchase price 320 → cash purchase price 313.60 → landed cost 325.60 → total cost 423.28 → cash selling price 465.61. Customer cash discount is calculated on the higher price: 465.61 / 0.98 = €475.11.

Backward calculation: a set of rims is to be offered for €500 net (list selling price). Customer discount 10%, customer cash discount 2%, profit 5%, overhead mark-up 25%. What is the maximum landed cost that can be paid?
500 − 10% = 450 − 2% = €441 cash selling price. Profit and overheads were added as mark-ups, so divide: 441 / 1.05 = 420 / 1.25 = €336.

Margin calculation: a set of complete wheels has a landed cost of €2,400, and the overhead mark-up is 35%. The market price is at most €3,300 net (no discounts). What is the profit as a percentage of total cost?
An accessory item is priced with a mark-up of 25% on landed cost. What is the gross margin (as a percentage of the selling price)?
The mark-up refers to the landed cost (100 → 125), the margin to the selling price: 25 / 125 × 100 = 20%.
A fleet customer offers 30 services at €180 net each. Variable costs are €140 and full costs €210 per service. The workshop has spare capacity. What should be decided?
Reject: there is a loss of €900
Accept: the operating result improves by €1,200
Accept: the operating result improves by €5,400
Reject: the price is below variable costs
Fixed costs are incurred anyway. The contribution margin decides: (180 − 140) × 30 = €1,200 extra.
A car wash has fixed costs of €36,000 a year. One wash earns €12 net, and the variable cost per wash is €3. At how many washes does it break even?
3,000 washes
2,400 washes
4,000 washes
12,000 washes
Break-even quantity = fixed costs / unit contribution margin = 36,000 / (12 − 3) = 4,000 washes.
Cash and cash equivalents €60,000, receivables €140,000, inventories €520,000, current liabilities €250,000. What is the quick ratio (2nd-degree liquidity)?
(Cash + receivables) / current liabilities × 100 = 200,000 / 250,000 × 100 = 80%. Inventories only count for 3rd-degree liquidity.
A dealership has €600,000 equity and €1,800,000 debt. What is the equity ratio?
Equity ratio = equity / total capital × 100 = 600,000 / 2,400,000 × 100 = 25%.
Profit €90,000, interest on debt €54,000, equity €600,000, debt €1,800,000. What is the return on total capital?
(Profit + interest on debt) / total capital × 100 = 144,000 / 2,400,000 × 100 = 6%.
Parts warehouse: opening stock €180,000, closing stock €220,000, cost of goods sold for the year €1,200,000. What is the average storage period (360 days)?
6 days
60 days
54 days
66 days
Average stock = (180,000 + 220,000) / 2 = €200,000. Turnover rate = 1,200,000 / 200,000 = 6; storage period = 360 / 6 = 60 days.
Target headcount 42, current headcount 38. Confirmed leavers: 3 (retirement and resignations). Confirmed joiners: 2 apprentices taken on. What is the net staffing requirement?
Net requirement = target − (current + joiners − leavers) = 42 − (38 + 2 − 3) = 5.
Which selection method puts several candidates through different exercises at the same time, such as role play, presentation and group discussion, assessed by several observers?
Structured job interview
Assessment centre
Personnel questionnaire
Work sample
An assessment centre uses several exercises and observers to test mainly social and methodological skills, e.g. for sales or service reception roles.

A service employee earns a gross salary of €3,200, including €40 employer savings contribution. Tax deductions are €410 and the employee's social security contribution is €680. The €40 savings instalment is transferred directly to the building society. What is the payout amount?
Net = 3,200 − 410 − 680 = €2,110. The savings instalment goes to the building society: 2,110 − 40 = €2,070.
The workshop has total annual costs of €1,080,000 and sells 12,000 hours. The profit mark-up is 8%. What is the net hourly labour rate?
Cost per hour sold = 1,080,000 / 12,000 = €90, plus 8% profit = €97.20.
A mechanics team is present for 1,600 hours in a month, of which 1,360 hours are clocked on customer jobs; 1,496 hours are invoiced. Which statement is correct?
Utilisation 110%, efficiency 85%
Utilisation 85%, efficiency 90.9%
Utilisation 85%, efficiency 110%
Utilisation 117.6%, efficiency 110%
Utilisation = clocked / attendance hours = 1,360 / 1,600 = 85%. Efficiency = invoiced / clocked hours = 1,496 / 1,360 = 110% (overall productivity: 1,496 / 1,600 = 93.5%).
From the dealership's point of view, what is an advantage of ordering new cars mainly against specific customer orders rather than for stock?
The customer receives the car faster
More cars are available for spontaneous test drives
No capital is tied up in unsold cars and there is no sales risk
The manufacturer generally pays higher stock bonuses for it
A car ordered for a customer is already sold. Stock cars tie up capital, cause holding costs and still have to find a buyer.
A manufacturer-owned branch (Werksniederlassung) is …
a sales outlet owned by the manufacturer that sells directly to end customers
an independent dealer with contractually guaranteed territorial protection
an authorised workshop that does not sell new cars
a wholesaler that passes vehicles on only to sub-dealers
Branches belong to the manufacturer's group and are part of direct distribution. The manufacturer bears the costs and risks itself.
Which question is an open question in the needs analysis?
Would you like a diesel again?
Would you like the car in white or in black?
Have you already had a test drive?
What will you mainly use the car for?
Open questions (W-questions) let the customer answer freely and reveal needs and buying motives. The others are closed questions or an either-or question.

According to the contract, a new car is to be delivered to a consumer two months after the contract is concluded. Before delivery, the manufacturer raises its list prices. May the dealership charge more on the basis of a price adjustment clause in its general terms and conditions?
Yes, if the manufacturer provides written proof of the increase
No, a clause allowing price increases for delivery within four months is invalid against consumers
Yes, but by no more than the inflation rate
Only if the customer finances the purchase price
Under § 309 No. 1 BGB, standard-term clauses providing for a price increase on goods to be delivered within four months of conclusion of the contract are invalid.
What does the eVB number prove at registration?
that comprehensive insurance has been taken out
that motor third-party liability insurance is in place
that the vehicle tax has been paid in advance
the EU type approval of the vehicle
The electronic insurance confirmation (eVB) is issued by the liability insurer. No vehicle can be registered without proof of compulsory insurance.
What does the EU certificate of conformity (CoC) certify?
that the buyer owns the vehicle
that the vehicle has passed its roadworthiness test
that the purchase price has been paid in full
that the vehicle conforms to an approved EU vehicle type
With the CoC the manufacturer confirms that the vehicle conforms to its EU type approval. It is the basis for first registration.
Which document must be carried when driving and shown on request?
Registration certificate part I
Registration certificate part II
EU certificate of conformity (CoC)
Purchase contract

Part I (vehicle registration document) must be carried under the vehicle registration regulation. Part II (vehicle title) should not be kept in the car because it is needed for sale and change of keeper.
When buying a new car, a customer wants to trade in a vehicle that is still financed. What must the dealership pay particular attention to?
A trade-in is legally impossible
The customer must first sell the vehicle privately
The outstanding loan must be paid off so that the dealership obtains ownership and registration certificate part II
The dealership automatically takes over the customer's loan agreement
The bank is usually the owner by way of security and holds part II. The dealership asks for the settlement amount, pays it off and offsets it against the trade-in price.
Why is professional reconditioning of used cars before sale worthwhile?
It extends the statutory liability for defects
It replaces the roadworthiness test
It makes defect disclosures in the contract unnecessary
It improves the first impression, shortens the holding period and raises the achievable price
A well-presented car looks more valuable, sells faster and thus reduces holding costs. Reconditioning does not change any legal obligations.
A dealership buys a car from a private individual for €10,000 and sells it under the margin scheme for €11,900. How much is the VAT?
Only the margin of €1,900 is taxed, and it is a gross amount: €1,900 × 19/119 = €303.36 (§ 25a UStG).
A dealership wants to shorten the limitation period for defect claims to one year when selling a used car to a consumer. What has been required for this since 2022?
The consumer must be specifically informed before the contract is concluded and the reduction must be agreed expressly and separately
A note in the terms and conditions on the back of the contract is sufficient
A reduction is never permitted with consumers
The buyer must also take out warranty insurance
This is laid down in § 476(2) BGB. Without the separate notice, the statutory period of two years applies.
A dealership buys several used cars from another dealership (commercial transaction on both sides). What must it do after delivery to preserve its rights regarding defects?
Nothing, liability for defects lasts two years anyway
Report defects at the latest before one year has passed
Inspect the vehicles without undue delay and give notice of any defects found without undue delay
Withdraw from the contract within 14 days
Between merchants, the duty to inspect and give notice under § 377 HGB applies. Anyone who does not give notice in time loses the rights for these defects because the goods are deemed accepted.
After the liability for defects and the manufacturer's warranty have expired, the manufacturer voluntarily pays half the cost of an engine failure. This is …
goodwill
a warranty service
liability for defects
product liability
Goodwill is a voluntary gesture with no legal entitlement. It serves customer loyalty and the brand image.
What applies when a financed vehicle is transferred by way of security (Sicherungsübereignung)?
The customer remains owner, the bank becomes direct possessor
The bank receives registration certificate part I
The bank becomes owner, the customer remains possessor and may use the vehicle
The vehicle is parked at the bank until the last instalment
The bank becomes owner by way of security and keeps part II, while the customer continues to use the car. After full repayment, ownership and part II return to the customer.
Which interest rate includes, in addition to the borrowing rate, other credit costs such as processing fees and is therefore suitable for comparing finance offers?
the borrowing (nominal) rate
the base rate
the default interest rate
the annual percentage rate (APR)
The APR expresses the total cost of credit as an annual percentage. It must be stated to consumers under the Price Indication Ordinance.
A consumer signs a loan agreement to finance a car at the dealership and is properly informed of the right of withdrawal. Can the consumer withdraw from the loan agreement?
No, because the contract was concluded on the business premises
Yes, within 14 days
Yes, within 7 days
Yes, within one month after handover of the vehicle

Consumer loans can be withdrawn from within 14 days regardless of where they were concluded (§§ 495, 355 BGB). With a linked purchase contract, the customer is then no longer bound by it either (§ 358 BGB).
Compared with an instalment loan without a final balloon payment, the same term and the same interest rate, what is a typical disadvantage of balloon financing for the customer?
higher monthly instalments
higher total interest costs because the balloon payment bears interest over the whole term
no right of withdrawal
the vehicle may not be registered
The balloon payment is only repaid at the end, so the outstanding balance stays high for longer. Monthly instalments are lower, but total interest is higher.
Under a residual value lease, the lessor sells the returned vehicle for less than the agreed residual value. Who bears the difference?
the lessee
the lessor
the arranging dealership
the manufacturer
In residual value leasing, the lessee bears the residual value risk and must make up a shortfall. Depending on the contract, any surplus is credited to the lessee in full or in part.
With otherwise identical terms, what is the effect of a higher initial lease payment (down payment)?
The calculated residual value rises
The term is extended
The lessee becomes owner at the end of the contract
The monthly lease instalments fall
The initial payment is an advance payment spread over the term. It lowers the instalments but strains liquidity at the start.
A customer who only has motor third-party liability insurance causes a rear-end collision. What does the insurer cover?
the damage to both vehicles
only the damage to the customer's own vehicle
the other party's damage, but not the damage to the customer's own vehicle
nothing, because the customer caused the accident
Liability insurance covers damage caused to third parties. Only comprehensive cover pays for damage to one's own vehicle.
A customer has an at-fault accident claim settled through comprehensive cover and has no no-claims protection. What usually happens?
Nothing, comprehensive claims do not affect the no-claims class
The policy ends automatically
The no-claims class is downgraded and the premium rises
Only the partial cover premium becomes more expensive
A settled comprehensive claim leads to a downgrade to a worse no-claims class the following year. For small claims, paying oneself can be cheaper.
An unknown person deliberately scratches the paint of a parked car. Under the usual model conditions (AKB), which insurance pays for the damage?
motor third-party liability
partial cover (Teilkasko)
the breakdown/assistance cover
comprehensive cover (Vollkasko)
Malicious damage by third parties (vandalism) is a comprehensive-cover claim. Partial cover includes theft, glass breakage, storm and collisions with game, among others.
A leased car is stolen. The comprehensive insurer pays the replacement value, but the lessor demands a higher settlement amount. What covers this gap?
GAP insurance
motor third-party liability
the breakdown/assistance cover
payment protection insurance

GAP cover pays the difference between the replacement value and the lease settlement or outstanding loan. Payment protection insurance, by contrast, applies e.g. in case of death or incapacity to work.
Which service is typically part of a motor assistance cover (Schutzbrief)?
Compensation for damage the driver causes to others
Roadside assistance and towing of the vehicle
Repair of at-fault accident damage
Refund of the purchase price after theft
Assistance cover provides help on the road such as breakdown service, towing, vehicle return or overnight costs. It does not cover damage to the vehicle itself.
Which CRM measure at a dealership mainly serves to retain existing customers?
timely contact before roadworthiness test, service and contract end dates based on customer data
buying third-party address lists for sales calls
discount campaigns only for new customers
deleting all customer data right after vehicle handover
CRM uses stored customer data to make suitable offers at the right time. Marketing contacts require the consent needed under data protection and competition law.
List price €200, 10% trade discount, 2% cash discount, delivery costs €6. What is the landed purchase price?
€200 − €20 discount = €180; − €3.60 cash discount = €176.40; + €6 delivery costs = €182.40.
Weighted scoring table: supplier A scores 5 points for quality (weight 40%) and 3 points for price (weight 60%). What is its weighted score?
4.0 points
4.2 points
3.8 points
3.4 points
Maximum stock 150 units, minimum stock 30 units. The delivery arrives exactly when the minimum stock is reached. What is the order quantity?
90 units
180 units
120 units
150 units
Order quantity = maximum stock − minimum stock = 150 − 30 = 120 units.
Commercial sale between two merchants: a material defect in brake pads, not detectable at goods-in inspection, appears after two months. What must the dealership do?
Nothing, the notification period has already expired
Notify the supplier without undue delay after discovery
Notify only once a customer complains about the defect
Notify the supplier within six months of discovery
Under § 377(3) HGB, hidden defects must be reported without undue delay after discovery; otherwise the goods are deemed accepted.
A dealership with three branches keeps all spare parts at one site and supplies the branches from there. This is a …
flow-through warehouse
central warehouse
third-party warehouse
decentralised warehouse
Central storage reduces stock and tied-up capital but lengthens the routes to the branches.
A parts store has an inventory turnover rate of 8. What is the average storage period?
80 days
36 days
8 days
45 days
Average storage period = 360 ÷ turnover rate = 360 ÷ 8 = 45 days.
Each item is counted once during the financial year; the stock on the balance sheet date comes from the continuous stock records. This is …
perpetual inventory
year-end stocktaking
shifted-date inventory
sample-based inventory
Perpetual inventory requires reliable stock records that capture all receipts and issues.
The dealership orders in response to a binding offer but demands an extra 5% discount in the order. Legally, the order is …
a new offer to the supplier
an order confirmation
a valid acceptance of the offer
a non-binding enquiry
An acceptance with changes counts as a rejection combined with a new offer (§ 150(2) BGB).
A supplier is late delivering ordered rims. The dealership wants to withdraw from the contract and buy elsewhere. What is normally required first?
Agree on a contractual penalty
Report the supplier to the chamber of commerce
Start court dunning proceedings
Set a reasonable additional deadline
Withdrawal and damages in lieu of performance generally require a reasonable additional deadline to have expired without result (§§ 323, 281 BGB).
A private customer complains to the dealership about a new alternator eight months after purchase. What is the burden of proof?
After six months there are no warranty rights left
The defect is presumed to have existed at handover
The manufacturer must prove the cause to the customer
The customer must prove the defect existed at handover
In consumer sales, for one year after handover the defect is presumed to have existed at handover (§ 477 BGB); the dealer would have to prove otherwise.
A business customer receives a workshop invoice with no agreed payment date. When, at the latest, is he in default without a reminder?
Immediately on receipt of the invoice
30 days after due date and receipt of the invoice
14 days after the invoice date
Only after the third reminder
This is set out in § 286(3) BGB; for consumers the 30-day rule only applies if the invoice points out this consequence.
A customer buys a roof box with base carrier. What should the salesperson definitely point out?
Observe the permitted roof load including carrier and box
The roof box must be entered in the vehicle documents
With a roof box, driving is only allowed in daylight
With a roof box, load securing is no longer required
The permitted roof load is stated in the owner's manual; carrier, box and contents together must not exceed it.
"Yes, these brake pads cost a bit more, but they last much longer." Which objection-handling method is this?
Yes-but method
Boomerang method
Pre-emption method
Counter-question method
The salesperson first agrees with the objection and then counters it with a benefit argument.
A customer wants to return defect-free, unopened wiper blades bought in the shop because he does not like them. What is the legal position?
He has a right to subsequent performance
He has a statutory 14-day right of withdrawal
No legal right; an exchange is a goodwill gesture
He has a right to a price reduction
A right of withdrawal only exists for distance and off-premises contracts; without a defect there are no warranty rights.
Does a workshop customer have to pay for a cost estimate?
Only if the estimate is non-binding
Always, because it takes working time
Only if the workshop is a master-craft business
Only if this was agreed beforehand
Under § 632(3) BGB, a cost estimate is not to be paid for unless otherwise agreed.
Why are brake pads always replaced per axle?
Because otherwise the brake fluid overheats
So that left and right brake equally hard
Because the periodic inspection requires it
So that the ABS does not need to be re-learned
Unevenly worn pads on one axle cause unequal braking, so the vehicle may pull to one side.
Since 1 October 2024, which tyres meet the winter tyre requirement in wintry road conditions?
All tyres with at least 4 mm tread depth
All tyres marked M+S
Only tyres with the Alpine symbol (mountain with snowflake)
All all-season tyres regardless of marking
The transition period for tyres marked only M+S expired on 30 September 2024.
The windscreen of a vehicle with a front camera has been replaced. Which work step is required afterwards?
Re-programming all of the vehicle's radio keys
Calibrating the front camera to manufacturer specifications
Entering the windscreen in the registration certificate
Changing the brake fluid to manufacturer specifications
Camera-based assistance systems such as lane keeping or emergency braking only work reliably with a correctly aligned camera.
Who may de-energise the high-voltage system of an electric vehicle?
Any apprentice from the second year onwards
A specialist qualified for high-voltage systems
Any employee after a short verbal briefing
The service advisor at vehicle reception
Work on the HV system requires special qualification under German accident-insurance (DGUV) rules; staff who are only made aware may carry out non-electrical work only.
What does a flexible service interval (longlife service) mean?
Oil changes are no longer needed for the vehicle's whole life
The inspection is done yearly regardless of mileage
The vehicle calculates the date from driving style and oil condition
The customer sets the date entirely as he likes
Sensors and software evaluate usage and operating conditions; an approved longlife oil is usually required.
Significant defects are found during the periodic technical inspection (HU). What follows?
Only a note in the report; the sticker is issued anyway
Vehicle is taken off the road immediately and must be towed
Sticker is issued; repair the defects by the next inspection
No sticker; repair the defects and have them re-checked within one month
The sticker is only issued after a successful re-inspection; if the one-month deadline is missed, a complete new inspection is required.
After an accident, liability is split 70:30 against the other party. What does the other party's liability insurer pay the customer?
100% of the damage
30% of the damage
50% of the damage
70% of the damage
Compensation follows the liability ratio; the customer bears the rest himself or via his comprehensive (fully comp) cover.
Which damage to one's own vehicle is typically covered by partial casco insurance?
A rear-end collision caused by oneself
Hail damage to roof and bonnet
Paint scratched by vandalism
A bollard scraped while manoeuvring
Partial casco covers fire, theft, glass breakage, storm, hail and collisions with game, among others; vandalism and self-caused accidents fall under fully comprehensive cover.
For a minor third-party liability claim, what is usually sufficient to quantify the damage?
A cost estimate from the workshop
A report by an independent appraiser
A verbal estimate by the customer
A damage estimate by the police
For minor damage, appraiser fees are considered disproportionate and are often not reimbursed; a cost estimate is enough.
The injured party in a liability claim rents an equivalent replacement vehicle. What is often deducted?
The deductible of his own comprehensive cover
Vehicle tax for the rental period
The cost of the damage report
Saved running costs of his own vehicle
Because his own car is not being worn during this time, a share for saved own costs is deducted; renting one class lower usually avoids this.
An injured party has a second car he can use without restriction and claims compensation for loss of use. As a rule …
There is no claim, as there is no noticeable loss of use
He gets double the daily rate because of two vehicles
He gets loss-of-use compensation and a rental car at once
His own casco insurer pays the loss-of-use compensation
Loss-of-use compensation requires the will and the possibility to use the car; an available second car usually rules out a noticeable impairment.
What is the purpose of a light-liquid (oil) separator in the workshop or at the wash bay?
It separates used oil from brake fluid for reuse
It filters brake dust from the air in the workshop
It keeps oil and fuel out of the waste water
It cleans exhaust gases during the emissions test
Light liquids must not enter the sewer system; the separator must be serviced and emptied regularly.
A round blue safety sign with a white symbol, e.g. safety goggles, is a …
emergency/escape sign
warning sign
prohibition sign
mandatory sign
Blue means mandatory action, red means prohibition or fire protection, yellow means warning and green means rescue/escape.
What typically belongs in a job posting but not in the job description?
Authority and deputy arrangements of the position
How to apply and the desired start date
Position of the job in the hierarchy
Goals and tasks of the position
The job description is an internal document about the position itself. How to apply and the start date are only needed in the posting, which addresses applicants.
